summary: PR #12 fixes reference links whose label contains a code span (`[`code`]`, `[`code`][]) by matching the label against the raw source of the definition. The fix is correct for the reported case and has no regression path I could find: the change can only turn previously unmatched lookups into matches. The full suite passes, flake8 is clean, and the changelog is updated. Remaining points are minor test-style and edge-case notes.
verified: Read the issue (#7) and the full diff; the change touches only changelog.md, inlinepatterns.py, treeprocessors.py and test_links.py.
Ran `python -m unittest discover tests` myself: Ran 1179 tests, OK (skipped=52).
Ran `python -m flake8` on the three changed Python files: no output (clean).

Probed `[`code`]` + `[`code`]: /url`, `[`code`][]`, mixed case `[`Code`]`, undefined `[code]` definition (stays unlinked, as before), `[text][ref]` plain text, and inline `[`code`](/url)`: all render as expected.
Probed multi-code-span labels (`[`a` `b`][]`), labels mixing emphasis and code (`[*x* `y`]`), double-backtick spans, and image references `![`code`][ref]` (alt="code"): all correct.
Probed HTML inside code spans in labels (`[`<b>`][]`): code text is escaped and the href/title come from the definition only; no escaping regression.

Reasoned through regressions: `raw_label` only changes the lookup key, and previously the key was a placeholder string that could never match a definition, so no previously-working link can stop resolving.

findings.issue: The new `TestCodeSpanLinkAcceptance` class uses `markdown.markdown(...)` with `assertIn` instead of the repo's `assertMarkdownRenders` convention, and its test names and docstrings embed internal acceptance-criteria IDs (AC-FR-001-1, AC-NFR-001-1) that mean nothing in upstream. It also overlaps with the tests already added to `TestReferenceLinks`.
findings.evidence: test_links.py:193-225 duplicate cases already covered at lines 437-552 (e.g. test_ref_link_code_span_text vs test_ac_fr_001_1_reference_code_span_label_becomes_link). assertIn passes even if the surrounding markup is wrong.

findings.issue: `raw_label` catches only KeyError. If an extension replaces the 'inline' treeprocessor with one that lacks `stashed_source`, this raises AttributeError on every reference label. Existing code at lines 238 and 533 has the same assumption about `stashed_nodes`, so this is a consistency nit, not a new hazard.

Not fixed and not tested: a code span containing `]` (or `\]`) in a label, such as `[`a]b`]` with a matching `[`a]b`]: /u` definition, still does not link. The cause is the definition regex stopping at the first `]` (blockprocessors ReferenceProcessor), not this change. It is outside the issue's scope, but worth a follow-up note.
findings.evidence:
Probe: markdown.markdown('[`a]b`]\n\n[`a]b`]: /u') renders `

[a]b]

` followed by the definition line as a paragraph.
